R2-01.why: Tagged evidence objects with discrete states and hotspot tables are sound and cheap. The hardest problem is the FREEZE! and catch-while-carrying checks: characters are client-owned, so the server sees movement 100-250 ms late and needs line-of-sight raycasts. Add the interior over-shoulder camera with wall fade (fiddly on mobile), ~40 objects x 4 visual states, 60 hotspots per house, and two asymmetric loadout trees, and this is a full mid-scope build.
R2-01.fix: Launch with one house and ~25 evidence objects and drop the Report Card 'funniest moment' AI in favour of 3 fixed stat cards. Make FREEZE a server snapshot of position deltas with a generous threshold, not velocity-in-view-cone.

R2-02.why: A kinematic spline raft (lateral offset, yaw, speed) does avoid physics-ownership problems and lets you cheaply record ghost rafts. The hardest problem is client prediction with 6 remote inputs: seated characters welded to the server raft will not match a client-predicted raft, so you need cosmetic character proxies or must accept about 150 ms of server-paced lag. Mesh water across ~30 joined segments and per-vehicle propulsion code (the balloon's altitude axis is effectively a second controller) add steady work.
R2-02.fix: Skip prediction: run the raft server-side at 20-30 Hz with client interpolation (latency is fine in a co-op party game). Launch with 2 vehicles and ~12 segments, and push Raft Race bumping and the balloon to updates.

R2-03.why: Mostly state machines plus cone raycasts, tagged prank targets and NPC pose cycling, all well within reach. The hardest problem is freeze/tag fairness under latency: the 0.3 s grace is shorter than a typical mobile RTT plus replication buffer, so the server must judge on movement history, not current velocity. Non-humanoid playable statues (T-rex skeleton) need custom rigs and animations. The 'Caught on Camera' reel implies a replay system.
R2-03.fix: Use R15 humanoid statues only at launch (mummy, knight, astronaut reskins) and make the grace at least 0.5 s, judged on server position history. Make the reel a set of still snapshot cards (ViewportFrame clones at prank time), not a recording.

R2-04.why: With no movement, no camera and a fixed scene, there is almost no networking or physics risk. A $1/Protractor recognizer for 6 bold glyphs is about 200 lines and can run on the server from ~32 resampled points, so trust is solved. The hardest problem is content and performance: 6 spells, 30 fusion VFX, misfires and wave enemies on mobile need CFrame-driven, non-Humanoid, client-rendered mobs. The 1 s fusion window must use server receive time, which is forgiving enough.
R2-04.fix: Launch with 10-12 fusions (not 30) and 3 enemy types plus 1 boss. Render enemies client-side from server lane-progress data, and cap ranked Trial leaderboards with server-side sanity checks.

R2-05.why: Low tech risk: UI (ViewportFrame inspection, drag-tool overlays), a role state machine, a touch log and Among-Us-style voting, all of it well-trodden. The hardest problem is content and balance: every item needs genuine/fake variants with tells per tool. 'Adaptive NPC forgers that learn' needs cross-server aggregation (MemoryStore/DataStore jobs) or is really manual weekly tuning. Social deduction with 4-8 players fails at low CCU because bots cannot credibly play forger or accuser.
R2-05.fix: Treat 'adaptive forgers' as a hand-tuned weekly rotation, ship ~30 items with 2 tells each, and make Open Shop PvE the default queue so low CCU still yields sessions. Cut the visitable museum to a profile shelf.

R2-06.why: The 6-primitive data-driven anomaly system is the most content-efficient design in the set, with one map and simple pings. The hardest problem is the CCTV feed: real ViewportFrame feeds are expensive and unlit, so the right approach is moving the Watcher's Camera and calling RequestStreamAroundAsync under StreamingEnabled. Per-role anomaly visibility must be client-rendered from server data, so exploiters can see everything (acceptable in co-op). The chase AI needs pathfinding.
R2-06.fix: Implement 'live feed' as moving the Watcher's camera, not ViewportFrames. Launch with one motel wing, ~20 signature anomalies plus the primitive generator, and a single chaser.

R2-07.why: The whole payoff depends on a 3D replay system. The hardest problem is recording ragdolls: they are not animations, so you need per-limb CFrames for about 15 parts per character, plus animation track IDs and time positions, ghost and prop state, and avatar reconstruction via HumanoidDescription. You also need event scoring to pick the 'best 30 s', and voice/screams cannot be captured on Roblox, which drains the Content Warning joke. Ghost AI variety and horror ambience come on top.
R2-07.fix: Keep the replay in the same server (no teleport payload). Record only HRP CFrame plus current emote/anim ID at 10 Hz with ragdoll as a canned 'dragged' animation, and replay only flagged event windows. Launch with 1 map and 4 ghosts.

R2-08.why: Per-parcel handling rules (sag, slosh, wake) computed from replicated character motion are noisy server-side, so they end up client-computed and trusted, which is fine in co-op. The hardest problem is the linked two-person carry: averaging both sticks server-side means taking control away from both characters (server ownership plus Humanoid:Move), giving RTT-delayed movement that feels bad. Physics-comedy expectations (revolving doors, dogs, toddlers) push toward real physics, which is what the concept is trying to avoid.
R2-08.fix: Make the linked carry a leader/follower tether (leader steers client-side, follower is constrained by a rope/AlignPosition and penalised for pulling against it). Ship 4 parcel types, scripted hazards only, and a hand-built street before procedural neighbourhoods.

R2-09.why: The auto-battler is a deterministic server sim replayed on clients: pure code, well suited to AI-assisted devs, with easy bot fill. The hardest problem is combinatorial critters: 150 visual mutations that also change attack patterns need a modular attachment-based rig plus procedural animation for odd body plans. Breeding and gifting critters between two players' DataStore keys is a classic dupe/rollback exploit vector that needs session locking and idempotent transactions. Balance across mutations is heavy design work.
R2-09.fix: Make mutations mostly cosmetic attachments with ~15 behaviour-affecting ones, and use tween/bob animation instead of rigs. Defer friend cross-breeding and gifting until the save system has session locking and a trade-ledger pattern (e.g., ProfileStore).

R2-10.why: Two players, UI-driven, turn-like state with trivial replication and no physics, characters or anti-exploit stakes. The hardest problem is a generator that produces solvable pictographic manuals from seasonal rule sets, and 25 module types is real volume, but each module is a small self-contained widget. Bot backfill as Book (auto-hints) is easy; bot as Hands is harder.
R2-10.fix: Launch with 8-10 modules plus the solo daily, ship the 3-player variant later, and have bots backfill only the Book role.

R2-11.why: Station mini-games and a cascading failure state machine are straightforward. The hardest problem is unstated: characters walking inside a CFrame-moved anchored vehicle are not carried by Roblox and slide or jitter, and a physics-driven ship reintroduces ownership problems. The right approach is a stationary interior with the world/sky scrolling past and the 'pilot yoke' only offsetting the scenery. Four vehicle types each need their own interior and stations.
R2-11.fix: Use a static-interior trick (move the world, not the ship) and launch with the airship only plus 3 routes. Make the landing a single timing mini-game and the crash a canned cutscene.

R2-12.why: Effectively two games: a co-op fire action game plus a visitable sanctuary with critter AI and decor placement (a housing system). Grid fire is fine server-side (coarse cells at 2-5 Hz, delta-replicated), but rendering hundreds of fire and smoke emitters on mobile, multi-floor procedural buildings with timed collapses, and pathfinding bots in a burning building are each substantial. The hardest problem is the content load: 120 critters needing rigs and animations for carry and sanctuary roaming, plus the two-person carry networking issue from R2-08.
R2-12.fix: Cut the launch to 1 building type (house) with 2 floors and 20 critters on a shared simple quadruped rig. Replace the visitable sanctuary with a read-only gallery and add placement later. Drop bots; allow solo play on smaller buildings.

overall_notes: Feasibility tracks with how little moving avatar-physics interaction each concept needs. Fixed-position or UI-driven concepts (R2-10, R2-04, R2-06) are clearly within a 2-5 person, 3-4 month scope. The recurring Roblox pitfalls are: (1) server judging client-owned character motion with tight windows (freeze in R2-01/R2-03, carry rules in R2-08), where latency of 150-300 ms on mobile breaks sub-0.5 s rules; (2) any 'two players control one thing' mechanic (linked carry, multi-seat raft), where server averaging means laggy controls unless one client leads; (3) characters on moving vehicles (R2-11, R2-02 seats), which need a static-interior or proxy trick; (4) replay systems (R2-07, and implicitly R2-03 and R2-01 highlights), which are always bigger than they look, so use snapshot cards. The stated approaches mostly hold: tagged evidence objects are good, the kinematic spline raft is good if prediction is dropped, grid fire spread is fine on the server but rendering-limited on mobile, gesture trust is solvable by classifying server-side, and CFrame replay at 10 Hz is OK for HRP but not for ragdolls. Social deduction (R2-05) and asymmetric 1vN (R2-01, R2-03) carry a hidden infrastructure cost at low CCU because bots cannot credibly fill key roles. Content volume (houses, critters, mutations, fusions, modules) is the main schedule risk across the board, more than code.
